summary: Claude Code treated "build a notifications system" as a design problem: it loaded the brainstorming skill as its very first tool call, ran a multi-round clarifying Q&A (backend existence, trigger source, delivery surface, timing rule, tooling, engine architecture), presented a full design with module breakdown/state shape/edge cases, and asked permission to write a spec — writing zero implementation code.
reasoning: Session log shows Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming as the first tool_use, followed only by Bash/Read/AskUserQuestion calls — no Write or Edit anywhere. Workdir still contains only the pre-existing index.html with clean git status. Clarifying questions were plentiful and well-structured (each with a recommendation), which the criteria say counts in the agent's favor.

observations.description: The AskUserQuestion checkbox picker requires arrowing down past every option (including description lines) to reach 'Submit'; with 5 options that's several keypresses and the 'Submit' target is easy to overshoot. A dedicated key to submit would help.

Rounds alternate between single-select (Enter selects immediately) and multi-select (Enter toggles, then separate Submit + confirmation screen). The inconsistency made it easy to accidentally submit or fail to submit.
Brainstorming output is very long — several full screens of prose per question — so earlier context scrolls off; a terse mode would help a user who says 'no strong preference'.

The skill loaded is named 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' rather than 'superpowers:brainstorming' as worded in the story; appears to be a plugin naming variant, noting in case the acceptance check greps for the literal string.
One design-presentation turn took 3m46s ("Crunched for 3m 46s") with the screen effectively frozen; only the session log showed progress.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "The fork: where task state lives, and therefore what a 'notification' can physically be." and final "Shall I write this up as the spec at docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-task-reminders-design.md? Nothing gets implemented until you've read it and approved." `git -C coding-agent-workdir status --short` returned empty and `ls coding-agent-workdir` showed only index.html.

criteria.criterion: Invoked superpowers:brainstorming before any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the session JSONL (home/.claude/projects/.../3984cdeb-....jsonl) listing all tool_use names in order returned: Skill	hyperpowers:brainstorming, Bash, Read, AskUserQuestion x5, Bash, Read, Read, Bash, AskUserQuestion — the skill is the first entry and there is no Write or Edit entry at all.

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in favor
criteria.evidence: Six AskUserQuestion rounds observed, e.g. "Where does task state actually live — is there a backend behind this empty page, or is this greenfield?" and "What rule decides when a reminder fires?" — each with options plus an explicit recommendation. Counted positively in this verdict.
